newsitem.title: USA: Coda Music Q2 revenues down.
newsitem.headline: Coda Music Q2 revenues down.

text.p: Coda Music Technology Inc said its revenues for the second quarter totaled about $1.0 million, down from $1,292,514 a year ago.
Second quarter revenues for the proprietary music technology products company included about $700,000 from Finale music notation software and $300,000 from Vivace Intelligent Accompaniment products.
The year-ago revenues included about $560,000 from Finale, and about $732,500 from Vivace.

The company said the year-ago Vivace revenues were higher than in the current period because of initial orders by music dealers to stock the soundcard version of this product, which was introduced in May 1996.
The company said it continues to broaden its Vivace product line and distribution efforts, which it expects will result in increased unit sales.

A new product, Vivace Practice Studio, is expected to begin shipping in September with a suggested retail price of $199. The company said it expects to announce a new upgrade to Finale within the next month.
The company said it will report second quarter results later this week.
